sourceTexts.sb30-gq3: 3- Why is climate important when traveling?
sourceTexts.sb30-a-instruction: A- Read the text and do the tasks below.
sourceTexts.sb30-reading-1: The difference between weather and climate is a measure of time. Weather is what the conditions of the atmosphere are over a short period of time, and climate is how the atmosphere changes over relatively long periods of time.
sourceTexts.sb30-reading-2: Sometimes the climate differs from one area to another in the same country, for example, Peru has a variety of climate types to choose where to go. It has the blue sky and sunshine of the tropical northern coast, the humid hot Amazon rainforest and the cold weather of the Andes, there is a climate to suit everyone’s taste in Peru. On the other hand, some countries have moderate, cold or hot climate all over the year. For example, Portugal enjoys a warm temperate climate with wet winters and dry summers.
sourceTexts.sb30-b-instruction: B - Decide if the statements are True or False.

sourceTexts.sb30-tf3: 3- The climate in Portugal is warm.

sourceTexts.sb31-instruction: Read the story and do the tasks below.
sourceTexts.sb31-story-1: Helen Adams Keller was born a healthy child in Alabama, on June 27,1880.
sourceTexts.sb31-story-2: At the age of 19 months, Helen became deaf and blind as a result of scarlet fever. As Helen grew from the time being a baby into childhood, she became wild. She would kick and scream when angry, and giggle when happy.
sourceTexts.sb31-story-3: Her family wanted their daughter to learn. They decided to help her and met the school's director who suggested a teacher who was called Ann Sullivan to work with Helen. Sullivan went to Keller's home in Alabama. Helen was six years old when Sullivan began to teach her finger spelling. She started by bringing Helen a doll to touch it and spell the word "doll".
sourceTexts.sb31-story-4: At first, Keller refused to cooperate with Sullivan's instruction. Finally, Sullivan asked Helen's parents to allow her with Helen alone, so that Keller could concentrate only on Sullivan's instruction. Therefore, Sullivan and Helen moved to a nearby cottage.
sourceTexts.sb31-story-5: After a great struggle with Helen, a surprising event happened. Sullivan taught Keller the word "water"; she helped her make the connection between the object and the letters by taking Keller out to the water pump, and placing Keller's hand under the water While Sullivan was flushing cool water over Keller's hand, she spelled out the word w-a-t-e-r. By nightfall, she had learned 30 words.
sourceTexts.sb31-story-6: Helen Keller overcame the difficult situation of being blind and deaf to become a famous American educator in the 20thcentury.

sourceTexts.wb14-reading-1: Hi, my name is Sandra, and I come from Lebanon. I like to visit historical places. I am going to Granada, Spain. Granada is a great place to visit. In the spring, you can ski in the mountains and swim in the ocean on the same day. It is a great place to walk. There are nice places to spend a sunny afternoon. Yaleton is a wonderful neighborhood. There are a lot of coffee shops, furniture stores, book stores and boutiques.

sourceTexts.wb16-a-pastperfect: is used to make it clear that one event happened before another one in the past.
